questions.prompt: According to higher-order theories, what makes a mental state conscious?

options.text: Being the object of a suitable higher-order representation, such as a thought that one is in that state
Being broadcast to many processes across the brain
options.why_wrong: Broadcast is the condition proposed by global workspace theory.

options.text: Generating a large amount of integrated information
options.why_wrong: That is the proposal of integrated information theory.

options.text: Being caused directly by a stimulus in the environment
options.why_wrong: Many unconscious states are also caused by stimuli; higher-order theories add a condition about representation.

questions.explanation: Higher-order theories hold that a state is conscious when the subject is aware of being in it, in virtue of a higher-order thought or perception about that state. Rosenthal's higher-order thought theory is a leading version.

sources.citation: Rosenthal, D. M. (2005). Consciousness and Mind. Oxford University Press.
Brown, R., Lau, H., & LeDoux, J. E. (2019). Understanding the higher-order approach to consciousness. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 23(9), 754-768.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blanks about higher-order theories.
questions.text: According to higher-order theories, a mental state is conscious when the subject has a suitable {{higher-order}} representation of being in it. In Rosenthal's version, this representation is a {{thought}}.
questions.explanation: Higher-order theories hold that a state is conscious when the subject is aware of being in it. In Rosenthal's version, that awareness is a higher-order thought.
